A little guidance

From marks to a morning. · Grade 2 · Parent answer key

Three gentle sessions: 15 minutes each. Understanding matters more than finishing every line.

Reading · 1
Strong evidence pairs: blank vs pictured page; missing vs present sentence; first marks vs finished lesson sheet. Two matching changes beat one lonely detail.
Reading · 2
Little first wondered if the marks were a secret. Comparing them with the finished morning lesson revised the inference: the marks were a plan to build a lesson.
Math · 1
19 − 12 = 7; 31 − 19 = 12; 12 − 7 = 5 (second change greater by 5).
Math · 2
14 + 9 = 23 before checks; 23 + 6 = 29 in all.
Math · 3
Claim false; 31 − 12 = 19.
Writing · sample
Sample: The blank page had no picture. I infer the jobs worked because the finished page shows a picture and a sentence.
These are imagined, enlarged scenes about how ordered instructions (code) can become a printed lesson — not a coding tutorial, IDE walkthrough, or claim about any one programming language. 'Instructions,' 'sequence,' and 'transform' are kid-sized models. The helper/computer is schematic. Job counts and morning totals are invented for math and independent of art scale. Screens and notebooks in the plates are props, not real interfaces to copy. Support pronunciation, invented spelling or dictation as useful. Keep adult guidance in this key or collapsed details.
Materials: pencil, crayons if you like, and scrap paper. Print kid pages separately from this key.
